key_insight: AToP converts Transformer attributions into visit-anchored temporal patterns that explain predicted readmission risk, rather than discovering cancer drugs.
clinical_relevance: Oncologic sequences such as cancer anemia followed by ascites contributed to higher predicted readmission risk, offering research insights rather than validated clinical guidance.
method: Compute per-token Integrated Gradients for a Transformer predicting 30-day readmission.
Mine frequent temporal patterns from salient events and collapse near-duplicates.
Summarize attribution among patients carrying each token or pattern.
evidence_signal: Using MIMIC-IV v3.1 data from 218,196 patients, the Transformer achieved AUROC 0.77 and PR-AUC 0.34; evaluation included masking, visit-order reversal, token-level faithfulness tests, and KernelSHAP comparison.
watch_item: Pattern attributions reflect model behavior, not unique causal effects or established clinical validity.
paper_title: AToP: An Explainability Framework for Transformer-Based EHR Predictions Using Attribution-Guided Temporal Pattern Mining
